Chapter 612 - Good Evidence, Bad Evidence
Father and Sakura-chan went to check out the shopping district.

That’s Itsuki’s take on things.
Hearing Father get praised makes me feel good too.

I’m not entirely sure where he’s going with this, but I nod along for now.

“So, you’re saying it’s important to learn the shop’s circumstances as well?”

If Itsuki’s logic were flawless, then as long as he gathered information properly, he wouldn’t have made mistakes.
And yet, he did.
Why is that?
Itsuki fell into deep thought once more in response to my question.
“Motoyasu-san, was there anything else Naofumi-san or the others warned me about in the first world?”

I have a vague sense that this is important information for keeping Itsuki from going off the rails.
If I can give him good advice here, maybe he won’t lose control.

Did Father, Big Sister, or anyone else say anything back then?

Ah, now that I think about it, I do recall Father and the others complaining… and I also remember my own thoughts on the matter.
“Rather than just gathering convenient evidence, wouldn’t it be better to also pay attention to inconvenient facts?”
Back then, when Father failed to convince Ren and Itsuki… I remember he said something similar about their strengthening methods.

Chapter 620 - Heartless

Chapter 622 - Jeers

Both would’ve ended up turning into voluptuous beauties like Filo anyway.
I mean, couldn’t he have just asked the slave trader to only push Raphtalia to me?
Motoyasu really is an idiot… well, it’s easy to say that in hindsight.
Actually, Raphtalia being so stubborn is part of the problem too.
Tracing it back… maybe it’s my fault?
Then, after being cornered by Motoyasu and not buying any slaves, he thought Raphtalia was stolen from him, like how far was he planning to push me?
To top it off, I didn’t buy any slaves and ended up looking like I was in a mutual love relationship with Sadeena, and showed through my actions that the world could be saved even without Raphtalia.
No wonder he hates Motoyasu.
Totally justified.
Too many pointless detours!
“It’s understandable why your relationship’s so strained. It must’ve been rough.”
“Yes, it was really hard!”
I feel deeply sorry for Raphtalia.
For now, I’ll just pat her head and comfort her.
I gently rub Raphtalia’s head.
“Rifana-chan, huh…”
Just as the mood started to lighten up a bit, Keel folded his arms and let out a groan.
Tch… When did he come back?
“Keel, you guys were supposed to be asleep. Don’t come back.”
“You guys were still talking, so I got curious and came back.”
The other slaves from the village nod in agreement.
“How’s she been doing?”
“Well… the last time I saw her, she gave me a push forward.”
“Rifana-chan was such a kind kid. Thinking about others more than herself—amazing.”
“Thinking about it makes me want to see her again… but we can’t anymore, huh?”
“Tomorrow, let’s go put flowers on the grave we all made. A visit for everyone, and for Rifana-chan.”
“You guys do that regularly since it’s close by.”
The graves of those originally from this village, including Raphtalia’s parents, have been made.
Everyone regularly cleans them and visits, so there are always fresh flowers.
“Rafuu.”
“I wonder what she looked like?”
“Umm…”
In response to my question, Raphtalia gestures to Raf-chan with open arms.
“Rafuu.”
Then, Raf-chan hops up and transforms.
Taller than Keel, shorter than Raphtalia, brown hair—she gives off a cute vibe.
“Ooh!”
The village slaves, including Keel, let out voices of awe.
“She really does look like Rifana-chan!”
“Amazing!”
“Rafuu.”
Well, even if she’s transformed, Raf-chan’s still Raf-chan. Can’t help that.
With a pop, Raf-chan stops transforming immediately.
“Come on, you guys, get to sleep. We’ve got more stuff lined up tomorrow.”
“Okay—”
And with that, the slaves head off.
…A strange silence falls over me, Raphtalia, and Raf-chan nearby.
“Like we talked about earlier, it must’ve been rough.”
“Yes.”
For Raphtalia, it must feel like she had to watch Rifana die twice.
Even if the second time was a proper farewell.
But… from what Motoyasu said, there’s the idea that even in death, the soul lingers to some degree, and the thing about Raphtalia being in a suspended state.
And then there were those ghost-like raccoon and weasel creatures we saw near Sadeena’s secret base.
Putting that together… maybe Rifana, who had lost hope in life, possessed Raphtalia in order to keep her alive—something like that flashes through my mind.
Well, maybe that’s a bit too convenient of a theory.
“Yeah… but it’s not all sad things. There were a lot of sad things, but also a lot of happy things, and that’s why we are where we are now.”
“I see…”
If Raphtalia thinks that way, then maybe it really is something to be happy about.
“Right, Raf-chan?”
Raphtalia gazes into Raf-chan’s eyes, tilts her head a bit, and smiles.
“Rafuu!”
Right… Raf-chan gives a happy cry, hops onto Raphtalia’s shoulder, and waves at me.
Just like Filo, huh? Hm?
…Wait, how does Raf-chan even know what Rifana looked like as she grew up?
Did Raphtalia tell her?
Now that I think about it, Raphtalia used to be a bit wary of Raf-chan, but that’s softened a lot.
“Well, let’s finish up the rest of the work for tonight. Naofumi-sama.”
“Ah, yeah… the next round of noisy ones will be here soon.”
Well… whatever.
“Rafuu!”
And like that, another night slowly passed.
